articles.title: ESR and CRP Testing in an Urban Emergency Department: Should We Still Be Doing This?
articles.abstract: Pediatricians in the Emergency Department frequently evaluate febrile children. To help identify the cause of fever and assess the severity of the underlying condition, practitioners often utilize erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein testing. While these markers of inflammation are deeply embedded in the practice of pediatrics, they were each developed more than 90 years ago, and their utility to current clinical practice is not well characterized. We conducted a 1-year retrospective study of children who underwent CRP and ESR testing at an urban Children's Hospital. We recorded and analyzed indications for testing, concordance between testing methods and metrics, including admission status and test performance, as reflected by sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios. ESR and CRP tests were frequently ordered in patients with clinically evident diagnoses. There were no cases of occult bacteremia, and patients with bacteremia typically had presentations indicative of bacterial infection. CRP was superior to ESR as a predictor of bacterial infection; however, the positive likelihood ratio was only 2.1. Combined testing was ordered for 39.4% of all CRP tests, and there was a high concordance (69.9%) between CRP and ESR testing. Combined testing offered limited incremental value for the detection of bacterial infections. CRP and ESR testing are currently overused in our Pediatric Emergency Department, providing limited diagnostic value while adding unnecessary hospital cost. Combined CRP and ESR testing provides limited incremental value. Stewardship of these testing modalities and an active reconsideration of how these tests are employed should be considered.

articles.title: Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers Presenting to a Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: To characterize the clinical presentation and management of anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 0 to 24 months presenting to a pediatric emergency department between June 2019 and June 2022 with concern for anaphylaxis. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and 10th Revision codes associated with anaphylaxis and confirmed to meet 2006 National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/Food Allergy and Anaphylaxis Network clinical criteria by chart review. Demographic and clinical information-including presenting symptoms, administered treatment, and patient disposition-were abstracted from the electronic medical record. Treatments of interest included epinephrine, antihistamines, corticosteroids, albuterol, and intravenous fluids. Data were analyzed descriptively. Among 225 potentially eligible encounters, we identified 155 patients who met inclusion criteria. Median age was 10.8 months (interquartile range: 8.4 to 15.6). Food triggered 96.1% of episodes. Skin and mucosal symptoms occurred in 99.4% of patients, gastrointestinal symptoms in 74.2%, respiratory symptoms in 57.4%, and cardiovascular symptoms in 5.8%. Intramuscular epinephrine was administered to 87.1% of patients, 90.4% of whom received a single dose. Most patients (88.4%) were discharged home, and none of those admitted required additional epinephrine. In this cohort, reactions were most often food-triggered and characterized by mucocutaneous symptoms with gastrointestinal and/or mild-to-moderate respiratory symptoms. Severe respiratory or cardiovascular involvement was uncommon. Symptoms tended to resolve after a single dose of epinephrine, and most patients were discharged home.

articles.title: Bystander AED Effectiveness Despite Low Utilisation in OHCA.
authors: Korean Cardiac Arrest Research Consortium (KoCARC) Investigators
articles.abstract: Observational estimates of bystander automated external defibrillator (AED) effectiveness are inconsistent in settings with mature public-access defibrillation infrastructure but low utilization, partly because the conventional reference group pools emergency medical services (EMS)-shocked with non-defibrillated patients. We estimated bystander AED effectiveness against a partitioned no-defibrillation reference, tested effect modification by location, and quantified the deployment-utilization gap. Retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) registry (Korea, October 2015-June 2025; 23,918 adults of presumed medical etiology). A three-tier prehospital defibrillation-provider variable was defined: bystander AED applied (n = 383); EMS-delivered shock without preceding bystander AED (n = 5,975); and no prehospital defibrillation (reference; n = 17,560). Primary outcomes were survival to discharge and good neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2), analyzed by multivariable logistic regression with propensity-score, inverse-probability-weighting and location-stratified secondary analyses. Bystander AED application was associated with improved survival (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.60; 95% CI 1.19-2.14) and good neurological outcome (2.31; 1.65-3.23), comparable to that of EMS-delivered shock; the pooled-control specification attenuated estimates to non-significance (survival 1.09; neurological 1.14). Shock-delivered applications significantly exceeded EMS-delivered shock for neurological outcome (aOR 1.43; p = 0.03). Effectiveness did not differ by location (interaction p ≥ 0.15). Bystander AED was applied in 8.5% of Public-area versus 1.9% of Nonpublic AED-opportunity cases-a 4.5-fold gap. Bystander AED was associated with improved outcomes when applied, comparable to or exceeding EMS-delivered shock; the dominant constraint was the deployment-utilization gap, greatest in residential settings. Residential rapid-activation infrastructure warrants policy priority alongside, not instead of, continued device placement.

articles.title: Supporting Mental Health in EMS Clinicians: A NAEMSP Position Statement and Resource Document.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians operate in environments characterized by repeated trauma exposure, operational unpredictability, shift work, moral distress, and cumulative occupational stress. A substantial body of evidence demonstrates elevated rates of post-traumatic stress symptoms, depression, anxiety, substance use, sleep disturbance, burnout, and suicide among EMS clinicians and other public safety professionals compared to the general public. The implications extend beyond individual well-being, affecting workforce sustainability, clinical performance, and high quality patient care. Mental health in EMS is therefore not solely an individual concern, but a systems issue. Therefore, the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) recommends that:Organizational leadership should recognize EMS clinician mental health as foundational to workforce sustainability and safe patient care.EMS clinician mental health awareness, management, and treatment options should be a core part of EMS education.EMS systems should take a multi-faceted approach to mental health, with an emphasis on ensuring access to confidential and culturally competent resources for EMS clinicians and other public safety professionals including telecommunicators, law enforcement officers and firefighters.EMS systems should engage in quality improvement to identify and improve practices affecting EMS clinician mental health.EMS systems should achieve meaningful and sustainable improvements in EMS clinician mental health through legislative advocacy and building strong partnerships with local, regional and national agencies including public health and research institutions.

articles.title: Consensus Guidelines for Prehospital Transfusion in Children: A Modified Delphi Study.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of early trauma-related mortality in children, yet implementation of prehospital blood transfusion (PHT) in children is heterogenous and without consistent guidance. Limited pediatric-specific evidence and physiologic differences from adults have contributed to substantial variability among existing emergency medical services (EMS) protocols. The objective of this study was to develop expert consensus recommendations for identifying pediatric patients who may benefit from PHT. We conducted a modified Delphi consensus study using a multidisciplinary panel of 20 experts in pediatric surgery, pediatric emergency medicine, and EMS medicine. Investigators compiled candidate criteria from existing PHT protocols and expert input. We conducted iterative electronic surveys to achieve expert consensus. We predefined consensus thresholds as ≥80% agreement for inclusion and <50% for exclusion. We employed descriptive statistics to summarize responses across rounds. The panel evaluated 208 candidate items and accepted 35 recommendations for inclusion over six rounds of voting. Consensus defined eligibility for PHT in children consisting of (1) known or suspected severe hemorrhage or major blood loss, (2) at least one indicator of shock following first-line hemorrhage control, and (3) EMS clinical judgment of the need for transfusion. Shock indicators included physiologic compromise, hemodynamic instability, poor perfusion, low cardiac output, or an abnormal validated pediatric shock index. Contraindications included do not resuscitate orders prohibiting transfusion and non-hemorrhagic shock. We were unable to reach consensus on routine inclusion of end-tidal carbon dioxide as an indication for transfusion. Experts came to consensus on pediatric-focused, pragmatic criteria to guide prehospital blood product transfusion in children. Implementation of these recommendations may reduce practice variability, support protocol development, and inform future prospective validation studies.

articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Inflammatory Pathways in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: This review aims to examine the role of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) in the pathophysiology of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), focusing on its contribution to inflammation, disease development, and clinical implications. Recent studies demonstrate that CHIP is enriched in HFpEF populations and is associated with increased disease risk and worse clinical outcomes. Mechanistically, CHIP promotes inflammatory signaling through activation of pathways such as the NLRP3 inflammasome and IL-1β/IL-6 axis. TET2 mutations, in particular, have been consistently linked to diastolic dysfunction and adverse remodeling, especially in patients with high inflammatory burden and cardiometabolic comorbidities. CHIP represents a novel link between ageing, inflammation, and HFpEF, contributing to disease heterogeneity and progression. It may serve as a biomarker for early detection, risk stratification, and patient phenotyping, while also offering potential therapeutic targets. Future research should focus on validating these findings and integrating CHIP into precision medicine approaches for HFpEF.

articles.title: Trailhead to Triage: A Backcountry Ski Workshop for Sharpening Clinical Decision Making in Emergency Medicine Residents.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDecision making in emergency medicine is influenced by cognitive bias, time pressure, uncertainty, and incomplete or unreliable feedback. Outdoor experiential learning may provide an environment in which these decision-making processes can be experienced and discussed in a practical context.ObjectiveThis study evaluated a novel outdoor experiential learning workshop designed to assess changes in emergency medicine residents' self-reported awareness and understanding of decision-making science.MethodsWe conducted a prospective single-cohort study of emergency medicine residents participating in an outdoor experiential learning workshop. Residents completed a 15-min asynchronous video lecture during the 2 wk preceding the field day, followed by guided backcountry activities incorporating structured discussions of decision-making science and clinical parallels. Participants completed surveys before and after the workshop and a 3-mo follow-up survey. Descriptive statistics and independent-samples t tests were used to evaluate changes in self-reported decision-making awareness and understanding.ResultsThirty residents completed the pre-intervention survey, 21 (70%) completed the post-intervention survey, and 22 (73%) completed the 3-mo follow-up. All measures demonstrated overall improvements from before to after the survey. The largest improvement was in understanding the importance of feedback in decision making (3.53±1.17 vs 4.38±0.74; P=0.001). This improvement maintained statistical significance at the longitudinal follow-up (3.53±1.17 vs 4.09±1.11; P=0.043), reflecting continued appreciation for the value of feedback in decision making.ConclusionsParticipants reported increased awareness and understanding of decision-making science following the workshop, with several measures remaining elevated at the 3-mo follow-up. Participants also reported high levels of enjoyment and perceived educational value.

articles.title: Opportunities for age-friendly emergency care: a mixed-methods study of older adult experiences in a Canadian Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to gain insight into the perceptions of care quality and ED experiences of older adults in a Canadian emergency department to develop targeted interventions to improve care experience and outcomes. This study utilized a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured phone interviews were conducted within 30 days of the index ED visit for 19 consenting participants. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data from interviews were coded using Nvivo software until thematic saturation was achieved. Surveys were administered to 120 older adults (65 years and older). The majority of older adults surveyed use the ED 2-5 times per year and primarily resided in an urban setting. Survey results identified that older adults were hungry and thirsty during their stay (56.7%), relied on care partners for help during their ED visit (29.2%), and the majority felt heard at triage (93.3%). Interview results identified four major themes and 12 subthemes, highlighting many challenges and opportunities in the care of older adults in the ED. Major themes were communication, care, facilities, and attitudes. While older adults expressed appreciation and general acceptance of current ED conditions, they highlighted several areas needing improvement, including enhanced communication from physicians, better privacy measures, parking accessibility, and improved accommodations for caregivers. This study highlights the unique challenges older adults face in the ED. While many expressed satisfaction and appreciation for their care, key areas for improvement emerged, especially in communication, privacy, and support services. Targeted interventions, such as geriatric friendly infrastructure and multidisciplinary teams, could improve care quality, patient satisfaction, and outcomes for older adults in the ED.

articles.title: Lessons learned while implementing a reusable orthopedic assistive devices recycling program in the pediatric emergency department.
articles.abstract: Lower extremity injuries are a common pediatric emergency presentation that require families to purchase crutches. These may not be affordable for many families, and crutches are often stored or discarded after treatment. There is a need for a solution to reduce the financial burden for families and medical waste. Using Quality Improvement methodology, our group implemented a reusable orthopedic assistive devices recycling program (ROAR) where crutches were dispensed for return and re-use in our pediatric emergency department. Our aim was to dispense 120 pairs, or at least 50% of crutches used in our department at no cost. After collaborative planning, an operational workflow was designed, and the program was launched in April of 2024. To date, 57 pairs of crutches were dispensed to families at no cost. 25 pairs of these crutches were returned at the time of submission. This represents a 44% return rate within the ROAR program. The program was well received by patients and staff, but faced barriers in recuperation of crutches, ultimately limiting its ability to meet our aim and increasing the cost of the program. Valuable progress was made including alleviating some financial strain on families in purchasing medical devices in our emergency department. In future iterations, adoption and staff buy-in should be maximized by emphasizing repeated education for staff, simple documentation and creative replacement of supplies including considering device donations.

articles.title: Emergency physicians' knowledge and practice in reporting medically unfit drivers in Atlantic Canada.
articles.abstract: Emergency physicians frequently encounter patients with medical conditions affecting their fitness to drive. Emergency physicians have legal and ethical duties to report medically unfit drivers. However, many report low confidence in making these decisions. This may lead to underreporting. We aimed to assess knowledge, practice, and barriers regarding reporting of unfit drivers by Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of emergency physicians from four Atlantic Provinces. The survey contained 62 questions across four categories: 1) Demographics (seven), 2) General knowledge (five), 3) Scenarios/practice (34), 4) Barriers/needs (16). Where appropriate, participants rated answers on a five-point Likert scale. Seventy-eight emergency physicians (response rate 20.6%) completed the survey: male (59.0%), age 35-44 (37.2%), formally trained in emergency medicine (74.7%). Overall, 88.5% lacked formal training to determine fitness to drive. Familiarity was low regarding provincial regulations (61.5% "slightly" or "somewhat" familiar) and the Canadian Medical Association Driver's guide (85.9% "not at all" to "somewhat" familiar) while most (80.8%) use clinical judgment to guide decisions. Half indicated they report (56.4%) and document (50.0%) unfit drivers only "sometimes" or less frequently. When presented with clinical scenarios where reporting is indicated (first seizure, recurrent seizure), most (100% and 96.2%) would advise the patients not to drive, but a third (33.4% and 37.2%) would either not report or leave it to another physician to do so. Lack of guideline knowledge was the most significant barrier to reporting, while pocket cards, an electronic app and electronic method to report were identified as enablers. Most emergency physicians (85.9%) would like formal education on this topic. Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians expressed low familiarity with guidelines for determining medical fitness to drive and disclosed potential underreporting. Efforts should focus on targeted education and streamlined tools to improve reporting and enhance road safety.

articles.title: Association between acute GFAP status and 6-month cognitive performance after mild traumatic brain injury: an exploratory follow-up study.
Clinical validation of the DRoPH score: a preoperative tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fractures.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Proximal humerus fractures are common injuries that are frequently associated with considerable technical challenges during surgical reduction and fixation. Although anatomical reduction is crucial for fracture healing and functional recovery, the anticipated difficulty of achieving satisfactory reduction is difficult to estimate preoperatively. The Difficulty of Reduction of Proximal Humerus Fractures (DRoPH) score was recently developed through a structured expert consensus process to estimate anticipated reduction difficulty based on predefined fracture- and patient-related characteristics. The aim of this study was to perform an initial clinical validation of the score. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent plate fixation of proximal humerus fractures at a tertiary trauma center between January 2014 and December 2024. DRoPH scores (0-10 points) were stratified into low (0-3), moderate (4-6), and high (7-10) difficulty categories. Validation was based on operative duration, postoperative reduction quality according to the criteria described by Schnetzke et al., and postoperative complications. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to assess the independent association of the DRoPH score with the primary outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, and surgical approach. Inter- and intra-rater reliability were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Of 1,012 patients treated for proximal humerus fractures, 392 met the inclusion criteria and had complete datasets available for analysis. Of these, 151 (38.5%) were classified as low, 186 (47.4%) as moderate, and 55 (14.0%) as high difficulty according to the DRoPH score. Operative duration increased significantly with increasing DRoPH scores, with an adjusted increase of 7.3 min per score point (95% CI 5.7-9.0; p < 0.001). Reduction quality deteriorated across difficulty categories, and higher DRoPH scores were independently associated with malreduction (OR 1.30 per point, 95% CI 1.12-1.50; p = 0.001). Overall complication rates increased from 15.2% in low-difficulty fractures to 34.5% in high-difficulty fractures, and the DRoPH score remained independently associated with complications in multivariable analysis (OR 1.15 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.28; p = 0.012). Inter- and intra-rater reliability of the overall DRoPH score were excellent (ICC 0.96 and 0.95, respectively). This study provides initial clinical validation of the DRoPH score as a reliable and clinically applicable tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fracture fixation. Higher DRoPH scores are independently associated with longer operative duration, increased risk of malreduction, and higher complication rates. The score may therefore serve as a useful adjunct for preoperative planning and risk stratification in surgically treated proximal humerus fractures. Further multicenter validation studies are warranted. Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Low-Acuity EMS Transport to the Emergency Department: An Observational Study Guided by the Andersen Behavioral Model.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) demand is increasing, with a growing proportion of low-acuity encounters. Prior studies are limited by regional sampling, inconsistent definitions, narrow observation periods, and limited theoretical grounding. The objective of this study was to identify predisposing, enabling, and need-based factors associated with EMS transport among low-acuity emergency department (ED) patients, guided by Andersen's Behavioral Model of Health Services Use. We conducted a secondary, retrospective observational study using a 10% random sample of multicenter electronic health record data from 21 EDs in the southeastern United States. Eligible visits included: 1) patient age >17 years, 2) occurred between January 1, 2016, and April 29, 2025, 3) triaged as Emergency Severity Index 4 or 5, and 4) ended in a final visit disposition of discharge. The primary outcome was arrival at the ED by EMS. We categorized independent variables as predisposing, enabling, or need-based factors according to Andersen's model. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 41,761 low-acuity ED encounters, 3,232 (7.7%) arrived by EMS. Higher odds of EMS use were observed for older age (per 10-year increase; aOR 1.33, 95% CI = 1.30-1.36), male sex (aOR 1.20, 95% CI = 1.12-1.30), being retired or disabled (aOR 3.60, 95% CI = 3.15-4.10), being unemployed (aOR 2.26, 95% CI = 2.04-2.52), having a nighttime presentation (aOR 1.63, 95% CI = 1.51-1.76), and mental health diagnosis (aOR 1.76, 95% CI = 1.62-1.90). Lower odds of EMS arrival were observed for white race (aOR 0.89, 95% CI = 0.83-0.96), established primary care (aOR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.53-0.62), weekend presentation (aOR 0.91; 95% CI = 0.84-0.99), and visits during (aOR 0.63, 95% CI = 0.55-0.71) or after (aOR 0.54, 95% CI = 0.48-0.61) the COVID-19 period. Rurality, insurance, and primary language were not associated with EMS use. Among low-acuity ED patients, EMS arrival was associated with older age, unemployment or disability, no established primary care clinician, and a previous mental health diagnosis. These characteristics identify a population that may be served by alternatives to ambulance transport, such as treat-in-place and alternative destination pathways, when paired with expanded access to primary care and behavioral health resources.

articles.title: Disaster Report: Military Helicopter Crash in a Deployed Environment - Providers' and Patient's Perspectives.
articles.abstract: The crash of a military helicopter during a 2023 United States Army deployment produced a mass-casualty incident (MASCAL) in an austere setting. One of the casualties was an Emergency Medicine (EM) physician who oversaw point-of-injury (POI) triage and early casualty evacuation with a Special Operations Forces (SOF) medic to the nearest Role II Military Treatment Facility (MTF), followed by movement of the six most severely injured patients to Role III, and subsequent transfer to Landstuhl Regional Medical Center (LRMC) via Critical Care Air Transport Team (CCATT). This disaster report explores the EM physician's actions as the initial provider, another EM physician as a receiving provider for a multi-leg fixed-wing transport, and a practicing trauma surgeon's unique perspective as one of the significantly injured patients. The viewpoints in this report highlight operational decisions including dispersion of medical assets, dynamic triage, destination/platform selection, and significant stressors of flight. Disaster care pathways should anticipate aeromedical stressors, emphasize patient positioning and communication, and align evacuation decisions with changing resources and injury patterns. These lessons are directly relevant to prehospital/disaster systems operating in contested, austere, or resource-limited environments.

articles.title: Association between the site of emergency care and patient-centered outcomes in patients with cancer: rationale and design of the French COVER cohort.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Patients living with cancer now account for a substantial and growing share of emergency department (ED) visits and carry a high burden of hospitalization and in-hospital death. Their acute presentations are frequently multifactorial - driven by disease progression, treatment toxicity, immunosuppression, or the decompensation of comorbid conditions. They may present with higher rates of complications because of novel therapies, such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and cellular therapies, whose emergency manifestations remain unfamiliar to many emergency physicians. Despite this growing importance, the unscheduled care of patients with cancer has received comparatively little dedicated research. How these patients are managed in the ED, how often the emergency physician can access the oncology medical record and goals of care, how the acute complications of new anticancer therapies present, and how a background of cancer should modify the diagnostic approach to everyday emergencies remain poorly characterized. To address these gaps, the Cohort of Onco-hematologic patients visiting the Emergency depaRtment was designed as a prospective, multicenter French cohort of consecutive adults with active cancer or in remission for less than 1 year, presenting to the ED for any reason. Enrollment took place across a national network of 76 EDs for two 1-week periods (summer 2025 and winter 2025-2026), with follow-up to 90 days, yielding a large sample of patients designed as a platform for multiple analyses. The primary aim of Cohort of Onco-hematologic patients visiting the Emergency depaRtment is to determine whether being managed in an ED located within the patient's own cancer referral center, rather than any other hospital, is associated with improvement in morbidity and mortality, captured by the number of days alive and out of hospital at 30 days. Beyond this primary aim, the cohort will support a broad research program on the place of the ED in the cancer care pathway, from patient profiling and pathway description to the emergency toxicities of anticancer drugs and the cancer-specific features of common presentations.

articles.title: Diagnostic Variability in the Modified Kocher Criteria for Septic Arthritis of the Hip: Implications for Aspiration Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the clinical application of the modified Kocher criteria (MKC) in assessing septic arthritis of the hip (SAH) at a tertiary children's hospital. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on subjects presenting to the emergency department and receiving a hip ultrasound over a 1-year period. Those without a hip effusion were excluded. Patient demographics, symptoms, imaging, labs, treatment, and final diagnoses were collected. SAH was defined clinically by the treating team, supported by patient presentation, lab/imaging findings, operative intervention, and antibiotic therapy. Descriptive and bivariate statistics based on variable distribution were used during analysis. A total of 326 subjects were identified, and 110 had effusion present on ultrasound. Eighteen (16.4%) underwent aspiration. Aspirated subjects had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores (P=0.001) and higher median values for all individual MKC components, including CRP, WBC, ESR, maximum temperature, and a higher prevalence of non-weight-bearing (P<0.05). SAH was diagnosed in 38.9% of the aspirated group (n=7), with MKC scores of 2 (n=2), 3 (n=3), and 5 (n=2). Aspiration rates increased across MKC scores 0 to 3, and synovial fluid inflammatory markers trended higher with increasing MKC scores. Thirteen subjects with an MKC score of 2 were not aspirated; final diagnoses included transient synovitis (n=9), hip effusion, osteomyelitis, sickle cell crisis, or limp (each n=1). Three subjects with an MKC score of 3 were not aspirated and later diagnosed with metastatic tumor, osteomyelitis, and rheumatic fever. Pediatric patients undergoing hip aspiration with a concern for SAH had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores and higher levels of all individual MKC components than their nonaspirated counterparts. However, nearly 15% of patients had MKC scores of 2 or 3 that were not aspirated in the ED, and SAH was identified even in lower-score subjects. While MKC scores appear to influence clinical decision-making, diagnostic variability remains. In patients with intermediate MKC scores of 2 to 3, the criteria should prompt further evaluation, taking into consideration the overall clinical context to guide aspiration decision-making.

articles.title: Similar Presentations, Divergent Clinical Courses: Pediatric Headache Care in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Pediatric emergency department (ED) headache presentations may follow heterogeneous clinical courses. To compare presentation characteristics, migraine order-set activation, pain-score change, treatment intensity, and health care utilization between pediatric ED headache encounters with and without a clinician-documented persistent/intractable headache. We conducted a multisite retrospective cross-sectional study of children aged 3 to 18 years presenting to 2 pediatric EDs with headache or migraine as a chief complaint from 2019 to 2023. Encounters were classified by clinician documentation of an intractable/refractory headache diagnosis or persistent symptoms despite initial treatment. The primary outcome was change from arrival to posttreatment/disposition pain score. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to each patient's first encounter and to clinician-documented migraine or status migrainosus. Among 529 encounters, 18.5% had a documented persistent/intractable headache course. Most presentation characteristics were similar, although symptom duration and pulmonary comorbidity differed. Order-set activation did not differ significantly (76.5% vs. 68.2%; P = 0.106). Encounters with a persistent/intractable headache had less pain improvement [median: -4 (interquartile range: -6.75 to -1) vs. -5 (interquartile range: -7 to -3); P = 0.002], received more medications, radiologic imaging (39.8% vs. 26%; P = 0.006), neurology consultation (56.1% vs. 39.4%; P = 0.003), hospitalization (19.4% vs. 3.2%; P < 0.001), and 30-day return ED visits (10.2% vs. 4.6%; P = 0.049). The pain-score difference was attenuated in the first-encounter analysis (P = 0.060), but persisted in the clinician-documented migraine subgroup (P = 0.006). Headache presentation characteristics and order-set activation did not distinguish the ED course, but pain improvement, treatment intensity, and utilization differed during ED care. Prospective studies should evaluate standardized early reassessment measures.

articles.title: Charting the rise of artificial intelligence in medical education: a global bibliometric and network analysis, 2000-2026.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral curiosity to a core feature of modern medical education through adaptive learning, simulation-based training, automated assessment, and large language models such as ChatGPT. Publication activity has accelerated rapidly, but the structure of this expanding literature has not been comprehensively mapped. Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy that combined medical education terms in the title field with artificial intelligence terms in the topic field. Articles, review articles, and data papers published from 2000 to 2026 were included. A total of 2,298 records were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analyses, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct keyword co-occurrence, country collaboration, and institutional collaboration networks. Data for 2026 represent a partial calendar year. Publication output remained limited until the late 2010s and rose sharply after 2021. Of the 2,298 records, 2,066 (89.9%) were published from 2021 to 2026, with the highest complete-year output in 2025 (821 publications). The United States led in publication volume (918 records) and raw citation count (14,582 citations), followed by the People's Republic of China (367 records; 4,404 citations). The Journal of Surgical Education published the most articles. Harvard Medical School led institutional output, whereas Stanford University and the University of California San Francisco had higher raw citation totals despite fewer publications. Artificial intelligence, medical education, ChatGPT, medical students, and machine learning were the most prominent keywords. Artificial intelligence in medical education is a rapidly expanding but geographically and institutionally concentrated field. Raw citation patterns differed from publication volume, although these unadjusted measures should not be interpreted as direct comparisons of research quality. Thematic patterns emphasize learner-facing applications, assessment, and generative AI, while responsible curricular integration and empirical evaluation remain important priorities. These findings are especially relevant to emergency medicine education, where simulation, time-sensitive decision-making, and competency assessment are central.

articles.title: Just the Facts: Management of patients presenting to the emergency department following therapeutic abortion.
Training and Use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) in Pediatrics and Neonatology in Latin America: A Multinational Survey Study.
articles.abstract: This study characterizes the current state of training, clinical use, and implementation barriers of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in Latin America. POCUS has become a fundamental diagnostic tool. However, limited information exists regarding its implementation in this region. A multinational cross-sectional survey study was conducted using an electronic survey administered to health care professionals caring for pediatric and neonatal populations across 21 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean (December 2025 to January 2026). We assessed the prevalence of formal training, frequency of clinical use, implementation barriers, and interest in further training. Analyses were performed using epidemiologically appropriate denominators. A total of 662 professionals were included, predominantly pediatric intensivists (45.2%) working in high-complexity settings (73.3%). Formal POCUS training was reported by 68.7%. Overall, 80.4% currently use POCUS; among them, 14.5% reported no formal training. Self-perceived unsupervised competence among trained participants was moderate. The most frequent clinical applications were pleural effusion and cardiac tamponade. The main barriers identified were lack of training (77.5%), limited access to equipment (50.5%), and absence of institutional protocols (48.9%). Interest in formal training was very high (92.9%). Substantial gaps remain in structured education, equipment access, and institutional protocol development. The significant proportion of untrained users and moderate self-perceived competence highlight an urgent need for standardized training programs. The high level of interest in training represents an opportunity to develop coordinated regional strategies to promote safe and effective POCUS implementation in Latin America.

articles.title: Epidemiology, clinical profile, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending at Spanish emergency departments (EDEN-56 study).
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Older adults with active cancer are increasing, clinically complex emergency department (ED) population, but large multicenter European data are limited. To describe the epidemiology, baseline characteristics, diagnoses, and outcomes of older patients with active cancer attending Spanish EDs, and assess whether associations between active cancer and short-term outcomes varied with age and sex. Secondary analysis of the Emergency Department and Elder Needs retrospective multicenter registry, including all patients aged greater than or equal to 65 years attending 52 Spanish EDs during 1-7 April 2019. Patients with and without active cancer were compared. Annualized incidence was extrapolated overall, by sex, and by age. Age-related patterns were modeled using restricted cubic splines. ED length of stay, hospitalization, length of hospitalization, and index-episode death. Age-by-cancer and age-by-sex interactions were assessed in unadjusted and multivariable models. Among 25 557 older ED patients, 4701 (18.4%) had active cancer. The estimated annualized incidence of ED presentations was 10 885 per 100 000 inhabitants aged greater than or equal to 65 years [95% confidence interval (CI): 10 576-11 200], higher in men (annualized rate ratio: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.70-1.91) and in the mid-to-late 80s. Patients with cancer had more severe comorbidity (58.9 vs. 12.9%), polypharmacy (26.6 vs. 21.3%), and walking handicaps (31.5 vs. 28.2%). Malignancy accounted for only 7.7% of ED diagnoses in the cancer group; infections, heart failure, and respiratory conditions were frequent. Active cancer was associated with longer median ED stay (4.0 vs. 3.3 h; adjusted difference: 0.3, 95% CI: 0.1-0.4), higher hospitalization [32.5 vs. 24.0%; adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.34, 95% CI: 1.25-1.44], longer median hospitalization (7.5 vs. 6.9 days; adjusted difference: 0.5, 0.1-0.9), and higher index-episode mortality (5.5 vs. 2.5%; adjusted OR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.81-2.50). Age significantly modified ED length of stay, hospitalization, and mortality, with significantly different age-related changes between patients with and without cancer. Among patients with cancer, age-related trajectories did not significantly differ by sex. Active cancer is common among older ED patients and associated with substantial resource use and worse short-term outcomes. These associations vary with age, supporting multidimensional assessment beyond chronological age or cancer status alone.

articles.title: Correction: Evaluation of pre-endoscopy risk scores and base deficit for prediction adverse clinical outcomes in patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Diagnostic performance and timeliness of ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy for peripheral lymphadenopathy in Internal Medicine: a multicenter real-world study.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) is increasingly used for evaluating peripheral lymphadenopathy, but evidence regarding its implementation in Internal Medicine remains limited. We assessed its diagnostic performance, safety, and diagnostic timeliness in routine clinical practice. This retrospective multicenter study included consecutive patients undergoing ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy in five Internal Medicine departments between February 2021 and March 2026. The primary outcome was diagnostic performance. Secondary outcomes included safety, diagnostic timeliness, performance in lymphoma patients, and factors associated with obtaining a definitive diagnosis. A total of 413 patients were included (median age 62 years; 41.3% women). Lymphoma and carcinoma accounted for 44.1% and 23.7% of final diagnoses, respectively. The first CNB provided a definitive diagnosis in 85.7% of patients and a suggestive diagnosis in 8.0%, yielding an overall diagnostic yield of 93.7%. No major complications occurred. Median time from biopsy request to procedure was 1 day (IQR 0-2), and median time to definitive diagnosis was 10 days (IQR 6-16). Surgical biopsy was required in 9.4% of patients and was associated with longer diagnostic delays (42 vs 9 days; p < 0.001). Among 182 patients with lymphoma, overall diagnostic yield was 93.4%. Lower operator experience and hospital size < 500 beds were independently associated with a lower likelihood of obtaining a definitive diagnosis. Ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy performed by internists demonstrated high diagnostic yield, excellent safety, and short diagnostic timelines in a large multicenter real-world cohort. Operator experience and institutional context may influence diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Renal trauma in a pediatric Level 1 trauma center: morbidity, mortality, and the role of renal scintigraphy.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Pediatric renal trauma is uncommon but potentially serious, and is often managed conservatively. Complications may occur, and the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up remains unclear. This study aimed to assess morbidity and mortality after pediatric renal trauma and to assess the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up. This retrospective single-center cohort study included pediatric trauma patients (< 18 years) with renal injuries admitted to a Level 1 trauma center in the Netherlands between January 1, 2001, and December 31, 2024. Mortality and in-hospital complications were assessed, and associations between renal scintigraphy abnormalities and complications during follow-up were evaluated. A total of 72 patients were included, of whom all injuries resulted from blunt trauma. Conservative management was applied in 88% of cases; embolization and nephrectomy were performed in 8% and 3% of patients, respectively. In-hospital mortality was 11% and was attributed exclusively to concomitant traumatic brain injury. Complications occurred in 25% of patients, primarily infections (19%), followed by hypertension during follow up (4%). Renal scintigraphy was performed in 53% of patients, predominantly in those with high-grade injuries; abnormalities were frequently observed (77%) but did not correlate with the occurrence of hypertension, proteinuria, or renal insufficiency during follow-up. Pediatric renal trauma, including high-grade injuries, can often be managed conservatively, and most complications can be treated using medical therapy or minimally invasive interventions. Renal scintigraphy showed no clear association with long-term morbidity and had limited additional value in routine follow-up. Given the potential for late-onset hypertension, structured long-term clinical surveillance with periodic monitoring of blood pressure, proteinuria, and renal function is warranted, particularly after high-grade injuries.

articles.title: Impella in infarction-related cardiogenic shock: evidence, complications, and implementation of microaxial LV unloading.
articles.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains highly lethal despite early revascularization. Although left ventricular (LV) failure predominates, AMI-CS may also be triggered or dominated by right ventricular (RV) failure, which carries distinct implications for the choice of mechanical support. Escalating catecholamines may increase afterload, provoke arrhythmias, and raise myocardial oxygen demand. Microaxial left ventricular (LV) support (Impella) provides forward flow while unloading the LV, potentially improving the subendocardial perfusion gradient, reducing pulmonary congestion, and limiting catecholamine exposure. Net clinical benefit is conditional and must be balanced against a substantial and predictable complication burden (major bleeding, vascular/limb complications, hemolysis with acute kidney injury, and infection). In the DanGer Shock trial, a protocolized Impella CP strategy in selected patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)-CS lowered 180-day mortality (45.8% vs. 58.5%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.74) but increased major complications and renal replacement therapy. Conversely, early venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO [extracorporal membrane oxygenation]) in the ECLS (extra corporal life support)-SHOCK trial did not improve 30-day survival and increased bleeding and vascular complications. Clinically, Impella should be used as part of phenotype-driven shock pathways-early for LV-dominant, congested low-output shock with a reversible trajectory-combined with standardized access/anticoagulation bundles, close complication surveillance, and early reassessment with deliberate escalation or de-escalation.

articles.title: Prehospital severity and in-hospital mortality in trauma patients managed by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia helicopter emergency medical service: a 6-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Data on in-hospital mortality among trauma patients managed by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) in Italy remain limited. We aimed to describe the epidemiology and in-hospital mortality of trauma patients transported after management by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia HEMS and to assess prehospital factors associated with death. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including trauma patients managed by HEMS FVG and transported to hospital, either directly by HEMS or after continuation of transport by ground emergency medical services, between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Jeffreys-prior penalized logistic regression was used to reduce sparse-data bias and instability from separation. The RTS-based model was designated as the primary model and the NACA-based model as a secondary sensitivity analysis. Model performance was assessed internally, and the functional forms of both age and RTS were examined using restricted cubic splines. Of 3,357 trauma records in the source cohort, 205 prehospital deaths were excluded from the in-hospital mortality analysis, leaving 3,152 transported patients. Outcome data were available for 3,143 patients, of whom 107 died in hospital (3.4%). In the primary RTS-based model, older age, lower RTS, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with mortality. Compared with RTS ≥ 7, adjusted ORs were 2.36 (95% CI 1.11-5.50) for RTS 4-<7 and 5.19 (95% CI 1.64-17.04) for RTS < 4. Age was associated with mortality (OR 1.03 per year, 95% CI 1.01-1.04). Continuous RTS analysis was concordant (OR 0.68 per one-point increase, 95% CI 0.54-0.86; p = 0.0013). Among trauma patients transported to hospital after HEMS management, older age, higher prehospital injury severity, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with in-hospital mortality. Intubation and CPR should be interpreted primarily as markers of severe physiological compromise rather than causal determinants of death.

articles.title: Flood Response in Rural Indonesia Implementing the World Health Organization Emergency Medical Team Minimum Data Set - Disaster Report.
articles.abstract: Indonesia experiences recurrent natural disasters that impose substantial strain on its health system, with annual flooding affecting rural communities such as Sitiarjo Sumbermanjing Wetan. Despite these recurring events, Indonesia has not systematically adopted the World Health Organization (WHO) Emergency Medical Team (EMT) Minimum Data Set (MDS) for standardized disaster medical reporting, thereby limiting data integration and evidence-based policy development. This disaster report describes the operational patterns, clinical demographics, and syndromic distribution captured by the WHO EMT MDS framework across three distinct flood responses in 2017, 2022, and 2023. The Universitas Brawijaya Emergency Medical Team (UB-EMT) prospectively collected daily surveillance data using the WHO EMT MDS reporting system. A total of 363 consultations were analyzed and stratified according to age, sex, and reporting period. Consultation volume peaked on Day 1 and declined on subsequent days. Females accounted for 62% of the cases and adults (18-64 years old) represented the majority of patients (68.87%). The most frequently reported conditions were skin diseases (33.46%), musculoskeletal problems (24.39%), and acute respiratory infections (16.64%), respectively. Age-specific patterns were evident: preschoolers and school-aged children presented with acute respiratory infections, whereas adults and older people more commonly experienced skin diseases and musculoskeletal problems. The absence of systematic implementation of the WHO EMT MDS constrains standardized surveillance and inter-team coordination in disaster settings. Therefore, the institutional adoption of the WHO EMT MDS is essential to strengthen real-time monitoring, optimize resource allocation, and enhance post-disaster evaluation in Indonesia.

articles.title: Impact of antithrombotic therapy on management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Antithrombotic agents are frequently implicated in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB), yet their impact on prognosis and management remains unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of pre-existing antithrombotic therapy on the management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB. This study used data from a retrospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients hospitalized for UGIB between January 2019 and December 2020 in Greater Paris University Hospitals. Patients were categorized into four groups according to their pre-existing antithrombotic treatment: antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulant therapy, both, or none. The primary outcome was thirty-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included endoscopy, endoscopic hemostasis, and blood transfusion within 7 days, and intensive care unit admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Among 928 patients, 226 (24%) were on antiplatelet therapy alone, 154 (17%) on anticoagulant therapy alone, 61 (7%) on combined therapy, and 487 (52%) received no antithrombotic treatment. Thirty-day mortality was 6.9%: 8.4% in the no-antithrombotic group, 6.2% in the antiplatelet group, 4.5% in the anticoagulant group, and 3.3% in the combined therapy group. Compared with the no-antithrombotic group, anticoagulant therapy alone was associated with lower mortality (aOR=0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.83), while antiplatelet therapy alone or combined therapy were not significantly associated (aOR=0.47, 95% CI 0.19-1.14 and aOR=0.12, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, respectively). Neither anticoagulant nor antiplatelet therapy was associated with secondary outcomes. Antithrombotic therapy had no negative impact on the management or prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

articles.title: A Robust Educational Initiative for EMS Clinicians Focusing on Pit-Crew CPR Improves Neurologically Intact Survival.
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether the implementation of a region-wide pit-crew cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) initiative was associated with improved survival to hospital discharge with good neurological function among adults with non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in a heterogenous, multi-agency emergency medical services (EMS) system in south-central Connecticut. We conducted a retrospective, before-and-after observational study using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES). The pit-crew CPR intervention, comprising structured didactic and hands-on simulation-based training was delivered across 27 EMS agencies from September 28, 2021 through August 2, 2022. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with good neurological function (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2). Secondary outcomes included survival to hospital discharge and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). We performed an interrupted time series analysis using the beginning of our intervention (September 28, 2021) as the interruption to model. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, race, shockable initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, arrest location, and bystander CPR. A total of 1917 adult non-traumatic OHCA patients (922 pre-intervention; 995 post-intervention) were resuscitated by EMS clinicians in the study period. In progression since intervention, there was a significant increase in neurologically intact survival per 4-month interval (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.44), suggesting a gradual improvement in outcomes over time after protocol implementation. At intervention start, there was a significant increase in ROSC (aOR 1.41; 95% CI, 1.1-1.81). There was no change in survival to hospital discharge prior to the intervention, at the time of the intervention, or following the intervention. Implementation of a pit-crew CPR model across a heterogenous, multi-agency EMS system was associated with a significant gradual increase in neurologically intact survival in the post-intervention period, as well as a significant immediate improvement in ROSC at the time of protocol implementation. These findings support structured, team-based resuscitation as a feasible and effective strategy to improve cardiac arrest outcomes within existing EMS systems.

articles.title: The Future of Cardiac Care: A Review on the Role for Non-Invasive, Home-Based Monitoring and Rehabilitation after Hospitalisation for Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is characterised by recurrent decompensation leading to worsening of symptoms and unplanned hospitalisations. Patients often experience poor post-hospitalisation recovery, fail to maintain functional capacity, and demonstrate a high risk for re-admission. In this review we discuss these challenges, and explore how non-invasive, digital solutions may improve health outcomes. In contrast to current episodic surveillance, advances in wearable sensor technologies enable continuous, non-invasive monitoring to facilitate physiology-guided management to improve early clinical stabilisation. Additionally, trials have highlighted the potential of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation to improve functional capacity in HF patients. Finally, continuous monitoring of relevant physiological signals, through developing algorithms, have the potential for early prediction of clinical deterioration. Non-invasive, co-created digital solutions may facilitate early stabilisation, improve functional capacity and predict clinical deterioration following episodes of decompensation. Collectively, they may enhance clinical outcomes and quality of life in patients with HF.

articles.title: Creation of a formal chest wall injury program improves compliance with rib fixation indications.
articles.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) improves outcomes but remains underutilized. This study evaluated the impact of the creation of a dedicated, institutional chest wall injury program on SSRF utilization, hypothesizing such a program would increase utilization of SSRF for those patients meeting criteria. We conducted a single-center, retrospective study of adults with radiographically confirmed rib fractures presenting to a Level I trauma center between January 2016 and April 2023. Patients were classified by the Chest Wall Injury Society SSRF operative criteria and whether or not they underwent SSRF. Basic demographics were obtained. The chest wall injury program was developed in 2020 with elements including standardized guideline adoption, daily multidisciplinary rounds to identify candidates early, and establishment of a dedicated outpatient follow-up clinic. Additionally, the program facilitated consistent documentation of SSRF candidacy and improved interdisciplinary communication regarding treatment plans. The primary outcome was the relationship between operative and non-operative cases when SSRF criteria were met. A total of 3488 patients were included, of whom 1629 met operative indications for SSRF. Overall, 457 patients (28.1%) underwent fixation. Compared to non-operative patients, the SSRF group had similar age and predominantly sustained blunt trauma. Implementation of the dedicated chest wall injury program in 2020 was associated with a significant increase in SSRF utilization among eligible patients, rising from 21.5% to 32.1% in 2020 (rise of 10.6%). Utilization continued to increase each subsequent year, reaching 45.3% by 2023. Among patients meeting SSRF criteria, SSRF utilization increased from 19.8% before 2021-41.1% from 2021 onward (p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age and gender, the 2021-onward period remained independently associated with receipt of SSRF (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 2.25-3.52; p < 0.001). Establishing a dedicated chest wall injury program was associated with higher adherence to SSRF guidelines and increased operative management of eligible patients. Level IV, therapeutic/care management.

articles.title: Epidemiological patterns and surgical outcomes of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a focus on domestic safety and seasonal variations.
articles.abstract: Supracondylar humerus fractures (SHFs) are prevalent pediatric elbow injuries. This study investigates the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes of pediatric SHFs to identify preventive strategies. This retrospective study included 298 pediatric patients (aged ≤14 years) treated for SHFs between December 2018 and June 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, seasonal variations, and surgical details were analyzed. Radiological reduction was assessed via the Baumann angle and anterior humeral line. Functional outcomes were evaluated using Flynn's criteria. The study cohort (mean age 6.1 years; 58.7% male) predominantly sustained extension-type fractures (96.3%), with the severely displaced Gartland Type III being the most frequent (49.3%). The incidence of injuries peaked during the summer months and school holidays, with the majority occurring at home (64.1%) due to simple falls (93%). Surgical intervention, consisting of closed reduction and percutaneous pinning, was necessitated in 75.8% of cases, with a mean time-to-surgery of 4.6 h. Satisfactory (excellent and good) functional outcomes were achieved in 97.9% of the patients. Overall complication rates were minimal, and transient nerve injuries (2%) fully resolved spontaneously during follow-up. Pediatric SHFs frequently occur in domestic settings during the summer months, strongly highlighting the need for "safe home" modifications and parental education. Despite a high prevalence of severely displaced fractures, prompt surgical intervention and meticulous anatomical reduction yield excellent long-term functional outcomes and minimize complications.

articles.title: Life-course hygiene exposures and disorders of gut-brain interaction: a multinational cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Despite growing interest in its role in immune-mediated diseases, the relevance of the hygiene hypothesis to disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations between childhood and adulthood hygiene-related exposures and DGBI prevalence, and to assess whether these associations persist after adjustment for sociodemographic and national development indicators. This cross-sectional study included 54,127 adults from 26 countries. DGBI were defined using Rome IV criteria. Childhood (≤ 7 years) and adulthood hygiene-related exposures included farm residence and access to running water, electricity, and rural residence. Country-level development was assessed using the Human Development Index (HDI). After adjustment for sociodemographic factors and psychological distress, several individual exposures showed independent associations with DGBI. Childhood farm exposure was independently associated with higher odds of DGBI (OR=1.11, 95% CI 1.03-1.19), irritable bowel syndrome (OR=1.21, 95% CI 1.03-1.42), and functional dyspepsia (OR=1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.38). In contrast, rural residence (OR=0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95) and absence of running water (OR=0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.90) or electricity (OR=0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.97) in adulthood were associated with lower odds of DGBI. These associations remained statistically significant after additional adjustment for HDI. Several individual hygiene-related environmental exposures were associated with DGBI, suggesting that environmental conditions may be associated with global variation in DGBI burden.

articles.title: Respiratory function, functional capacity, dyspnea, and sleep quality in young adults using the IQOS heated tobacco product: a matched cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: This matched cross-sectional study compared respiratory function, respiratory muscle strength, functional exercise capacity, dyspnea, and sleep quality between young IQOS users and matched control subjects. This study involved 31 young adult IQOS users and 31 age/sex/body mass index-matched never-tobacco users who underwent a standardized testing protocol during a single visit. Spirometry, maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), 6-min walk test (6MWT), modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale, modified Borg Scale (mBorg), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores were compared. While mean resting lung functions were similar between groups (all p > 0.05), IQOS users had shorter 6MWT distances (591.1 [580.2 - 638.4] meters vs. 626.0 [600.5 - 683.8] meters, p = 0.003, r = 0.53) and higher mMRC dyspnea scores (median mMRC Grade = 1 (0-1) in IQOS users vs 0 (0-0) in controls, p < 0.001, r = 0.62), higher mBorg dyspnea scores at the end of the 6MWT (median end-6MWT mBorg rating scale 1 [0-2] vs 0 [0-1], p = 0.001, r = 0.57), and poor sleep quality (PSQI global score 6.32 ± 2.63 vs 4.58 ± 1.61, p = 0.012, r = 0.45). Additionally, while MIP values tended toward being lower in IQOS users, these differences were statistically nonsignificant (p = 0.090). In conclusion, young exclusive IQOS users showed lower functional exercise capacity, greater dyspnea, and poorer sleep quality than matched never-users despite comparable resting spirometry, and these hypothesis-generating findings warrant longitudinal evaluation with biochemical exposure verification.

articles.title: Assessing health advocacy competencies through a novel simulation OSCE-based educational framework.
articles.abstract: Health advocacy remains one of the least explicitly assessed CanMEDS roles in Emergency Medicine. Objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) simulation is used to assess performance in real time but has not previously incorporated social determinants of health. We developed and piloted a simulation-based OSCE, embedding advocacy within acute clinical care and introduced novel assessment tools, completed by both examiners and standardized patients. Here we report the feasibility and acceptability of this OSCE and assessment tools. Twenty-two residents completed the advocacy and standard cases; 18 (82%) completed exit surveys. Most participants did not know advocacy would be assessed. Participants described the case as realistic and acceptable with minor suggestions for refinement. Assessors found the assessments intuitive to use and feasible to implement. This pilot suggests structured assessment of patient-level advocacy from both physician and patient perspectives can be feasibly integrated into simulation assessment without disrupting usual performance evaluation.

articles.title: Performance of updated American College of Surgeons field triage guidelines in identifying need for trauma center care.
articles.abstract: The Guidelines for the Field Triage of injured patients were updated in 2021 to improve the reliability of prehospital trauma triage. The objective of this study was to describe the association of the 2021 Field Triage Guidelines criteria with need for advanced trauma center care from a cohort of patients transported to a level 1 trauma center. This was a health records review of Field Triage Guidelines criteria met for trauma team activations at a level 1 trauma center from January 2020 to December 2021. Hospital-based and injury severity score (ISS)-based trauma center need were defined and sensitivity and specificity of the Field Triage Guidelines calculated for both. Area under the receiver operator curves were used to assess accuracy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association of each criterion with trauma center need. A total of 1427 patients were included and 90.3% met at least one Field Triage Guidelines criteria. Overall, patients meeting hospital-based trauma center need was 33.8% compared to 28.4% which met ISS-based trauma center need. Field Triage Guidelines criteria demonstrated a sensitivity of 97.3% and specificity of 13.3% with respect to hospital-based trauma center need with an area under the ROC of 0.80. Mental status and vital signs showed the highest association with trauma center need. The updated 2021 Field Triage Guidelines demonstrate good accuracy when assessed retrospectively on a cohort of patients transferred to a level 1 trauma center. The very high sensitivity of the new guidelines may help to reduce undertriage rates to the international goal of <5%. New criteria in this iteration of the Field Triage Guidelines could lead to improved rates of undertriage specifically in severely injured geriatric patients.

Surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity is associated with early adverse outcomes after major emergency abdominal surgery: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Intraoperative complexity in major emergency abdominal surgery lacks a standardized definition and is rarely quantified prospectively. Whether surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity is associated with short-term postoperative outcomes remains unknown. In this single-center prospective cohort study, 411 patients undergoing major emergency abdominal surgery were included. Immediately after surgery, the operating surgeon rated perceived intraoperative complexity on a 0-10 scale. The association between surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity and the primary outcome, 30-day unplanned reoperation, was investigated using Fine-Gray regression. The model was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, performance status, and intraoperative pathology. Secondary outcomes were 30-day mortality, length of stay, and Comprehensive Complication Index. Unplanned reoperation occurred in 15% and 30-day mortality in 11%. Higher surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity was associated with reoperation (sHR 1.20 per point; 95% CI 1.08-1.34). Complexity was also associated with prolonged LOS (β 1.47 days per unit increase; 95% CI 0.93-2.01), higher CCI category (OR 1.24 per unit increase; 95% CI 1.14-1.35), and increased 30-day mortality (OR 1.25; 95% CI 1.07-1.45). Surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity was associated with reoperation, morbidity, and 30-day mortality after major emergency abdominal surgery. These findings suggest that the operating surgeon's assessment may capture clinically meaningful prognostic information beyond conventional baseline risk factors. External validation and evaluation of inter-rater reproducibility are needed before clinical implementation.
