articles.title: Feasibility of Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality-Brief Intervention in an Emergency Department With Youth Who Are Suicidal.
articles.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) are key entry points for many youth experiencing suicidal thoughts and behaviors into mental health care. ED clinicians play a critical role in crisis intervention, prevention, and linking patients to ongoing care, yet many report uncertainty when assessing for and managing suicidal risk. The Collaborative Assessment and Management of suicidal thoughts and behaviors [Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS)] is an evidence-based, suicide-focused intervention that has been adapted into a single session [CAMS-Brief Intervention (CAMS-BI)]. This study tested the use of CAMS-BI with youth who are suicidal and presenting to a pediatric ED. Participants (aged 12 to 21 y; n = 20) were approached in the ED and completed distress measures before and after CAMS-BI. Following standard discharge timelines was prioritized. Analyses supported CAMS-BI's feasibility for ED youth populations, given the observed low rate of intervention refusal (8.7%) and high completion rate (87%). Participation in the study did not delay ED discharge times. Youth receiving CAMS-BI reported significantly lower distress postintervention, d = 0.45. Three-month follow-up indicated reductions in ED-return rates (0%) compared with youth who did not receive the intervention (15%), and strong patient engagement with outpatient treatment following CAMS-BI was notable (88% attended follow-up appointment). This pilot study provides evidence for CAMS-BI's feasibility for youth in fast-paced ED settings and its clinical value to quickly decrease distress. Future directions include larger, more rigorous replications to fine-tune CAMS-BI implementation into ED workflows.

articles.title: Autonomy in Fellowship Training and Its Influence on Self-Reported Self-Efficacy in Pediatric Emergency Medicine.
articles.abstract: This study examined the relationship between autonomy during pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellowship and self-efficacy in 6 Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education-defined entrustable professional activities (EPAs). We hypothesized that experiencing greater autonomy during fellowship would correlate with higher self-efficacy among current fellows and recent graduates. An anonymous electronic survey was distributed to current (2021-2022) second- and third-year PEM fellows and first- and second-year PEM attendings who graduated in 2020 and 2021. The survey collected demographic data, self-reported levels of autonomy during fellowship, and self-efficacy ratings for each EPA on a 0 to 100 scale, assessed both currently and retrospectively for 1 year prior. Autonomy was defined as ≥33% of clinical time in indirect supervision or independent practice. Statistical analyses included paired t tests, independent t tests, and multivariate analysis of covariance. One hundred twelve current fellows and 86 recent graduates responded (39% response rate). Both cohorts reported significant self-efficacy improvements across all 6 EPAs over the assessed period (P<0.001 for all comparisons). No significant differences in self-efficacy gains were observed between those who reported experiencing autonomy during fellowship and those who did not (P>0.05). In multivariate analysis, prior self-efficacy was the only consistent predictor of current self-efficacy (P<0.0001), explaining 53% to 71% of variance. This study found no association between self-reported autonomy in PEM fellowship training and self-efficacy in PEM-specific EPAs. Self-efficacy increased over time among all respondents regardless of autonomy experience. These findings suggest that the relationship between autonomy and trainee development may be more complex than previously assumed and warrants further investigation with refined measurement tools.

articles.title: Nitrous Oxide Use in Autistic Children: A Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract: Describe the population of autistic children who undergo nitrous oxide sedation and the rate of associated adverse events (AEs). Analyze patient- and procedure-level factors associated with AEs in autistic children receiving nitrous oxide outside the dental setting. A retrospective, descriptive study of autistic children, 3 to 18 years, who received nitrous oxide for procedural sedation during an emergency department or sedation encounter within a single hospital system between January 2014 and December 2023. Data extracted included patient demographics and comorbidities, as well as indication, maximum concentration, duration of administration, and AEs of nitrous oxide. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data. Analysis was performed on 186 patients [median age: 8 years (interquartile range: 5.2-12.75), 74.2% male]. Intravenous line placement was the most common indication in all locations. Most received 70% nitrous oxide with a median duration of 6 minutes (interquartile range: 4 -9.75). AEs were rare, occurring in only 3 patients (1.6%), with zero vomiting or aborted procedures. Given the rarity of AEs, no associated factors were able to be identified. Nitrous oxide is a safe, effective, and well-tolerated option for procedural sedation in autistic children, with a low rate of AEs. These findings add to the limited literature supporting its use in nondental settings and suggest it may be a valuable tool for facilitating minor procedures in this population. Future prospective studies are needed to optimize nitrous oxide delivery and determine factors contributing to AEs.

articles.title: Food Insecurity Screening and Immediate Access to Prepackaged Groceries in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Food insecurity (FI) is prevalent in many urban settings across the United States. Many vulnerable families who lack access to a medical home utilize the pediatric emergency department (PED), making the PED a critical access point to address FI. We aimed to understand caregivers' experiences in receiving prepackaged groceries and community resources within a PED. In this pilot initiative, caregivers who screened positive for FI in the PED received prepackaged groceries for their household and a list of community resources. Caregivers were interviewed to understand their experience in receiving food resources in the PED. Phone interviews were conducted until code saturation was reached. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and coded. Content analysis generated themes describing the impact of the intervention. This study was conducted in a tertiary care PED in an urban setting between October 2018 and June 2019. Participants included English-speaking caregivers of children younger than 18 years. Ninety-six households received groceries and a list of community food resources. Four themes emerged from interviewing 23 caregivers: (1) immediate food relief was helpful when their child was acutely ill, (2) caregivers generally accepted the food from the prepackaged bags, (3) community resources were difficult to access, and (4) FI households who did not use community resources ascribed this to a lack of need for urgent food. Families perceived benefits of being provided groceries during emergency department visits since there are barriers to accessing community resources.

articles.title: Repeat 9-1-1 Calls and Clinical Outcomes of Children After Non-transport by Emergency Medical Services.
articles.abstract: Pediatric non-transport by emergency medical services (EMS) is common but there are limited data assessing patient outcomes. Our primary objective was to determine the proportion of children not transported by EMS who have a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. Our secondary objective was to determine whether patient demographic or clinical characteristics are associated with repeat 9-1-1 call and transport. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the 2018-2022 ESO Data Collaborative research dataset. Of these records, one third are linked to hospital data which allowed for inclusion of discharge and ICD-10 diagnosis codes for some of the cases. We used descriptive statistics to compare cases (non-transported children aged 0-17 years with repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h) to controls (no repeat 9-1-1 call or repeat 9-1-1 call with non-transport). We conducted a multivariable logistic regression analysis to evaluate factors associated with a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. We generated descriptive statistics summarizing emergency department (ED) dispositions for the subset of patients where this data was available. Of 1,849,925 pediatric 9-1-1 calls, 732,525 (40%) were not transported by EMS. Within 72 h, 7,544 (1%) had repeat 9-1-1 call with transport to the ED. Repeat 9-1-1 call was associated with young age (0-4 years), Black, non-Hispanic race, male sex, calls from areas with a very low Child Opportunity Index (Opportunity Index), calls during out-of-office hours, and neurologic primary impressions. There were 11 (0.1%) deaths on scene upon repeat 9-1-1 call within 72 h of initial non-transport. Of the 1,001 (13%) patients with hospital-linked data, 814 (89%) were discharged from the ED, 162 (16%) were hospitalized, and two (0.2%) died. Only 1% of children not transported by EMS had a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. Hospitalization and death after non-transport were rare. These results may inform the development of safe and efficient pediatric non-transport protocols.

articles.title: Practice Patterns and Performance of Pediatric Air Medical Tracheal Intubation: A National Multisite Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Pediatric prehospital advanced airway management is high-stakes and low-frequency. Prior analyses have been limited to single-agency air medical groups or ground emergency medical services cohorts. National air medical performance is not well described. The aim of this study is to characterize practice patterns and outcomes of pediatric air medical intubation across a national multisite cohort. This was a retrospective cohort study of pediatric (<18 years) intubation encounters performed by air medical crews and recorded in ImageTrend Collaborate, a multisite prehospital clinical data repository, from 2021 to 2025. First-pass success, overall intubation success, and post-attempt physiology defined as a composite of hypoxia, age-adjusted hypotension, and age-adjusted bradycardia within 10 min after index attempt were summarized as n(%) or median (interquartile range [IQR]) and compared across four age groups (<1, 1-5, 6-10, 11-17 years) using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Site-level medication use was summarized among sites contributing 10 or more encounters. Among 1,040 encounters from 39 contributing sites across four United States regions, median age was 13 years (IQR 5-16) and 57.7% involved trauma or burn. A sedative-plus-paralytic strategy was used in 77.8% (809/1,040) with ketamine the most common induction agent (43.5% ketamine-only, 31.9% etomidate-only). Video laryngoscopy was documented in 8.6% of intubations. First-pass success was 86.5% (898/1,038) and overall success was 93.3% (968/1,038). Performance varied significantly by age with first-pass success at 69.1% (47/68) in infants under 1 year versus 88.7% (535/603) in adolescents (p < 0.001), overall success 80.9% (55/68) versus 93.9% (566/603), respectively (p < 0.001), and post-attempt physiologic instability 53.6% (30/56) versus 31.3% (175/560) respectively (p = 0.008). Post-attempt end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) within 10 min was documented in 82.8% (861/1,040) overall, and 60.0% (42/70) in infants (p < 0.001). Among the 13 sites with 10 or more encounters, peri-attempt ketamine share ranged from 9% to 84% and succinylcholine share from 0% to 91%. In this national multisite air medical cohort, overall airway performance was favorable, but infants younger than 1 year had lower first-pass success, lower overall intubation success, and less frequent post-intubation ETCO2 documentation. Substantial practice variation across contributing sites suggests opportunity for both targeted training in the infant subgroup and benchmarking across sites.

articles.title: Prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a widespread condition affecting individuals globally in the aftermath of disasters. For this review, the disaster-affected population refers to individuals or populations who have experienced a potentially traumatic event with psychosocial consequences. The current review aims to assess the prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in the present study. Relevant keywords were identified and used to search databases, including Scopus, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane, as well as websites and reference lists, to identify eligible studies. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow chart was used for the final included studies to reveal the results. The current review conducted a critical appraisal of the included studies by using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality evaluation. Meta-analysis using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP) software and manual analysis was done to assess the psychosocial factors and conceptual framework. A total of 1370 documents were identified from the databases, and 151 documents were duplicates. Following title/abstract screening, 1178 studies were excluded, 21 full text not retrieved, and 20 studies were included for the final results. The critical appraisal results found that more than half of the studies demonstrated good methodological quality. The results revealed that the pooled prevalence of PTSD was 38%, with young populations disproportionately affected, although no significant associations were found with age group, disaster type, or region. Nineteen psychosocial risk factors were identified, prominently including loss of family members or pets and property damage. The conceptual framework highlights the interplay between traumatic events and psychosocial factors in PTSD outcomes. The findings underscore the need for multidisciplinary collaboration among mental health professionals, long-term intervention strategies, and evidence-based practices to address India's mental health challenges.

articles.title: Exercise, Nutrition and GLP-1 Medicines to Improve Body Weight and Muscle Function in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on lifestyle, pharmacological, surgical, and multimodal interventions targeting muscle strength, body composition, and functional capacity in HFpEF with sarcopenia and/or obesity. Exercise, particularly concurrent endurance and resistance training protocols, improve aerobic capacity, functional performance, symptoms, and quality of life in HFpEF. Protein supplementation may preserve muscle mass, while caloric restriction may enhance aerobic capacity and function butdecreases muscle mass. SGLT2i and GLP-1 medicines may reduce hospitalizations and improve symptoms, with GLP-1 medicines producing greater weight loss and performance benefits. Bariatric surgery may also achieve substantial weight loss and functional improvements, although evidence in HFpEF with obesity is limited. Obesity-related HFpEF may benefit from a combination of resistance exercise and adequate protein intake to preserve muscle during weight loss, while pharmacotherapy can be used to support cardiac function. Future trials should evaluate multimodal interventions to mitigate frailty risk in HFpEF.

articles.title: Injury patterns in a war zone: A comparative analysis of civilians and military personnel.
articles.abstract: Modern armed conflicts increasingly affect both civilians and defense forces, resulting in heterogeneous injury patterns driven by diverse mechanisms. Direct comparative data between these populations treated within the same healthcare system remain limited. To compare injury mechanisms, anatomical injury patterns, injury severity, and early clinical outcomes between civilians and defense forces casualties treated at a single tertiary trauma center during an active conflict. A retrospective analysis was conducted of all consecutive war-related trauma admissions between October 7, 2023, and January 7, 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, anatomical sites, Injury Severity Score (ISS), emergency interventions, and early outcomes were collected. Percentage-based comparative plots were used to visualize injury mechanism and anatomical site distributions. The cohort included 192 patients (128 defense forces, 64 civilians). Civilians were older and included more females. Overall injury severity and rates of airway management, ventilatory support, and ICU admission were comparable between groups. Defense forces more frequently required direct transfer from the emergency department to the operating room (28% vs. 14%, p = 0.047). Shrapnel-related injuries were significantly more common among defense forces, whereas acoustic trauma was observed exclusively among civilians (36%, p < 0.001). Injury-mechanism profiles differed between groups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the proportions of patients injured at the individual anatomical site. Despite similar overall injury severity, civilians and defense forces exhibit distinct injury profiles. Civilians are disproportionately affected by acoustic trauma, highlighting population-specific vulnerabilities with implications for triage, diagnostic evaluation, and trauma system preparedness, especially during mass casualty incidents, when rapid recognition of group-specific injury patterns is essential for appropriate resource prioritization and allocation.

articles.title: Force measurement in circular external fixation frames reflects construct stability: A laboratory proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: Circular external fixation frames are widely used in limb reconstruction, however determining the optimal time for frame removal remains challenging. Current approaches rely on clinical and radiological assessment, both of which have recognised limitations. Mechanical assessment of construct stability offers a potential alternative, but existing approaches have not translated widely into clinical practice, in part due to reliance on absolute measurement thresholds. To determine whether force measurement within a circular external fixation frame varies systematically with fracture site stability, and to assess whether this measurement may support monitoring of healing progression. Three similar four-ring Ilizarov frame constructs were assembled using a Perspex bone analogue. A load cell was integrated into the frame and used to measure force during axial loading to 700 N. Models representing different stages of fracture healing were simulated using varying fracture gaps and materials of differing stiffness. Measurements were obtained across multiple sensor positions and configurations. Force measurements were compared between models using non-parametric statistical methods. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess separation between conditions. Force measured within the frame decreased progressively with increasing construct stiffness. A significant relationship between model stability and measured force was observed (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.0001). Clear separation was demonstrated between grossly unstable and intact constructs; however, overlap between higher stability models and intact bone was evident. ROC analysis showed strong discrimination when considering all unstable conditions (AUC ≥ 0.91), but performance was reduced when restricted to higher stability models (AUC 0.699-0.838). Absolute force measurements varied with sensor configuration, although the rank order of conditions was preserved. Force measurement within a circular external fixation frame reflects construct stability in an in vitro model. Whilst absolute values are dependent on construct configuration and show reduced discrimination near union, consistent directional changes suggest that serial within-subject measurement may provide a useful approach to monitoring healing progression. These findings support further evaluation of longitudinal measurement strategies in clinical studies.

articles.title: Screening for posttraumatic stress symptoms after accidental injury: Implementation of the young child PTSD screen in the acute trauma setting.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) in young children are underrecognized following unintentional injury, and validated screening tools for early childhood are rarely implemented in acute trauma settings. We evaluated the Young Child PTSD Screen (YCPS) administered at hospital discharge to determine screening positivity, associated clinical factors, and persistence of symptoms at one month. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 2-6 years admitted to a Level I pediatric trauma center following unintentional injury (November 2020-November 2024). Caregivers completed the 6-item YCPS at discharge. Children with ≥ 1 endorsed symptom were contacted one month later for repeat assessment. Demographic, injury, and hospitalization data were abstracted from the trauma registry and electronic health record. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated predictors of positive screening at discharge, and follow-up analyses assessed persistence of symptoms. Of 193 screened patients, 186 met inclusion criteria. Over half (55.9%, n = 104) screened symptomatic or positive at discharge. On univariate analysis, greater injury severity score and longer length of stay were associated with symptomatic/positive screening. In multivariable analysis, injury severity remained the only significant predictor (aOR 1.07 per point increase in injury severity score, 95% CI 1.02-1.13, p = 0.004). Of eligible children, 32.6% (n = 34) completed one-month follow-up and 41.1% (n = 14) screened positive. Higher discharge YCPS scores were associated with positive follow-up (median 3 vs 2; p = 0.046) and were positively correlated with one-month scores (r²=0.21, p = 0.005). No demographic variables (age, sex, race) predicted persistence of symptoms. Over one-third of traumatically injured young children screened positive for PTSS at discharge, and a substantial proportion had persistent symptoms at one month. Injury severity was associated with positive screens at discharge, while early symptom burden predicted persistence. These findings support the feasibility and clinical value of implementing developmentally sensitive screening for very young children in the inpatient trauma setting.

articles.title: Patterns of multimorbidity and in-hospital kidney function decline in older adults: a latent class analysis of three acute-care cohorts.
articles.abstract: Multimorbidity is associated with an increased risk of renal function decline in older individuals. In this study, we aimed to evaluate whether multimorbidity patterns differently contributed to this risk in three different hospital settings. We conducted a comparative cohort study of patients aged ≥ 65 years admitted to acute-care hospitals in Italy. Data were drawn from the retrospective SIN-SIGG study (geriatric units, n = 1600; nephrology units, n = 560) and the prospective REPOSI registry (internal medicine units, n = 4595). Quantitative multimorbidity was defined as the number of chronic conditions with prevalence ≥ 5% per cohort; qualitative multimorbidity was derived through latent class analysis of disease combinations. The primary outcome was change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from admission to discharge, calculated using the Berlin Initiative Study 1 (BIS1) equation. A relative decline was defined as ≥ 20% reduction from baseline. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, baseline eGFR, acute diagnoses, and number of medications. Among 6,755 patients (mean age 80.6 years; 47% women), multimorbidity prevalence ranged from 87 to 93%. Quantitative multimorbidity showed modest and inconsistent associations with renal decline. In contrast, qualitative multimorbidity consistently predicted eGFR deterioration. Across all cohorts, the cardiorespiratory and renal cluster was associated with higher odds of in-hospital eGFR decline compared with neurogeriatric and mixed patterns (geriatrics OR 2.24 [95% CI 1.16-4.70]; internal medicine OR 1.72 [95% CI 1.22-2.45]; nephrology OR 2.11 [95% CI 1.01-4.56]). Disease-pattern-based multimorbidity better stratifies short-term renal risk than disease counts, identifying high-risk patients for targeted nephroprotective care during hospitalization.

articles.title: Dietary sodium density as a potential nutritional marker of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis in Korean adults: a nationwide cross-sectional study with a dose-response analysis.
articles.abstract: The association between energy-adjusted dietary sodium density and non-invasively assessed hepatic steatosis remains poorly defined in population-based studies. We investigated the association and dose-response relationship between dietary sodium density and HSI-defined hepatic steatosis in Korean adults. We analyzed 14,445 adults (aged ≥20 years) from the 2021-2023 KNHANES. Sodium intake from a 24-h recall was calculated as sodium density (mg/1,000 kcal). HSI ≥36 defined hepatic steatosis; descriptive analyses compared HSI <36 versus ≥36, whereas regression analyses used HSI <30 as the reference, with HSI 30.0-35.9 treated separately. Compared with HSI <30, each 100 mg/1,000 kcal increase in sodium density was associated with higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis across all models: Unadjusted OR 1.058 (95% CI 1.032-1.085; P<0.001), Age/Sex-adjusted OR 1.051 (95% CI 1.024-1.079; P<0.001), Lifestyle-adjusted OR 1.048 (95% CI 1.020-1.077; P=0.001), and Fully adjusted OR 1.054 (95% CI 1.020-1.089; P=0.002). Participants in the highest sodium density quartile (Q4) exhibited 36.2% higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis than those in the lowest quartile (Q1) (adjusted OR 1.362; 95% CI 1.144-1.621; P=0.0004; P for trend = 0.001). The association remained robust after adjusting for potassium density (OR 1.042; 95% CI 1.012-1.072; P=0.005). RCS analysis showed an approximately linear increase in odds across the observed range, without evidence of non-linearity (P=0.738). Elevated sodium density was associated with higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis and may serve as a nutritional marker of metabolic liver health.

articles.title: The challenges and opportunities of major trauma care in Germany - results of multidisciplinary expert interviews of the LeAf trauma study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: The recovery process of major trauma survivors involves various sectors within a complex system of different medical service providers and stakeholders who accompany and support patients throughout the recovery pathway. The aim was to explore experiences and opinions of experts, who are actively involved in the care of major trauma patients in the German healthcare system. Semistructured in-depth group interviews were used to investigate experiences and opinions of experts with the focus on exploration of expert perspectives on opportunities and challenges of the cross sectoral care. An exploratory analysis was performed with an artificial intelligence-based coding software. In a second step, a system map was developed, and all inter- and intra-sectoral challenges and all opportunities for the optimization of processes were mapped. 39 experts from 13 medical specialties and occupational groups who were interviewed highlighted that intersectional issues especially across and within sectors pose a significant challenge to patient care. Four challenges were highlighted that significantly influence patient care: (1) Communication between sectors; (2) Complexity of transitions between sectors; (3) Inadequate aftercare and (4) Lack of psychosocial care. In conclusion five key learnings can be derived which could help to transform the healthcare system towards a system in which the complex condition major trauma with its high potential of chronification is enabling patients towards living a self-determined life and is creating opportunities for patients to return to work: (1) interdisciplinary collaboration (2), improved communication (3), early psychosocial screening and intervention (4), continuity of care (5), involvement of relatives.

articles.title: Peri-periprosthetic femoral fractures: a single-centre case series of a rare and challenging clinical scenario.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are an increasingly common complication of hip arthroplasty. A poorly defined scenario is a new femoral fracture after a previously treated PFF has united, which we term a peri-periprosthetic femoral fracture. We retrospectively reviewed 154 surgically treated PFF episodes in patients aged over 65 years at our institution between 2011 and 2021. A peri-periprosthetic fracture was defined as a new acute femoral fracture after documented radiographic union of a previously treated PFF. Clinical, surgical, and radiographic data were reviewed. Seven patients (4.5% of the institutional PFF cohort) met the criteria. Mean age was 83.1 years and 6 (85.7%) were female. The mean interval to the peri-periprosthetic fracture was 37.3 months (median 27; range 7-105). By the Vancouver classification, 3 fractures were type B1, 1 type B3, and 3 type C. Treatment was individualised to fracture configuration, prosthetic stability, hardware, and bone stock. Radiographic union was documented in all 4 patients with adequate follow-up, at a mean of 4.3 months. Five patients regained ambulation; one with pre-existing limitations did not, and ambulatory status was unavailable for one. Medical complications occurred in 2 patients, and no major orthopaedic complication required reoperation. Mortality was 14.3% at one year and 42.9% at two years. Peri-periprosthetic femoral fractures constitute a rare and technically demanding scenario, distinct from delayed union, nonunion, refracture through an incompletely healed fracture, and fixation failure. Treatment should be individualised to prosthetic stability, pre-existing hardware, fracture morphology, and residual bone stock.

articles.title: In-hospital mortality in hip fracture patients undergoing surgery later than 24 hours post admission might rather reflect the impact of comorbidities and treatment limitations than additional risks imposed by the mere timely delay itself.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Early surgery for proximal femoral fractures is widely recommended, but the association between surgical delay and short-term mortality remains uncertain because observational studies are vulnerable to confounding by patient characteristics and treatment limitation. We retrospectively studied adults with operatively treated proximal femoral fractures at a DGU-certified regional trauma center in Germany (2022-2025). Time to surgery was measured from emergency department registration to operative start. Delays > 24 h were classified as medical or non-medical where sufficiently documented. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Adjusted analyses included age, sex, ASA category, fracture type, concomitant orthopaedic injury, and treatment limitation (DNR/DNI; not time-anchored to surgery) and used Firth penalized logistic regression. Among 927 patients, 871 (94.0%) underwent surgery within 24 h; 53 (5.7%) died in hospital. Crude mortality was 5.6% after surgery within 24 h and 7.1% after surgery > 24 h. After adjustment, no clear independent association between surgery > 24 h and mortality was detected (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 0.29-2.92). Higher age, male sex, advanced ASA class, and treatment limitation were associated with mortality. In exploratory analyses, mortality was 19.0% among medically delayed patients and 0% among patients with non-medical delay, but adjusted estimates were highly imprecise. No clear association between surgery beyond 24 h and in-hospital mortality was detected after adjustment for measured patient characteristics and treatment-limitation status. The estimate was imprecise and compatible with clinically relevant benefit or harm; these findings do not establish the absence of an effect of surgical delay.

articles.title: Reporting of Sociodemographic and Equity-Related Factors in Emergency Department Pain Trials for Children: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Effective management of children's acute pain in emergency departments (EDs) is essential, yet health disparities exist. The applicability of evidence to diverse pediatric populations depends on clear demographic reporting. The PROGRESS-Plus framework identifies social determinants of health that influence care and outcomes, but it is unclear to what extent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in pediatric ED pain management report these variables. This scoping review examines the frequency and completeness of PROGRESS-Plus reporting in RCTs evaluating acute pain interventions for children in EDs in Canada and the USA. Using Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the Participant, Concept, Context framework, we conducted a scoping review of RCTs published between 2013 and 2025. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and CENTRAL were searched using a peer-reviewed strategy. Eligible studies involved children and youth experiencing acute presenting or procedural pain in ED settings. Two reviewers independently screened studies. Data were extracted using standardized forms refined with input from patient partners. Narrative synthesis and descriptive statistics were applied to summarize PROGRESS-Plus reporting. Of 3667 records identified, 65 RCTs met inclusion criteria. Thirty-five studies focused on procedural pain interventions, and 30 on interventions for painful presentations. Age was reported in all studies, and gender and/or sex in 98%. Race and/or ethnicity was reported in 40%, and chronic illness and/or disability in 18%. No studies reported socioeconomic status or place of residence. RCTs addressing pediatric pain in the ED rarely report equity-relevant demographic variables beyond age and gender and/or sex, limiting assessment of intervention effectiveness across diverse populations. Standardized demographic reporting is needed to support equitable, evidence-based pain research and care.

articles.title: Prehospital Minithoracostomy versus Chest Drainage for Emergency Pleural Decompression in Major Trauma.
articles.abstract: Prehospital pleural decompression is life-saving in patients with suspected tension pneumothorax or other life-threatening thoracic pressure pathology after major trauma. Although prehospital minithoracostomy (PHMT) is increasingly adopted by physician-led helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS), comparative evidence with prehospital chest drainage (PHCD) remains limited. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of consecutive adult trauma patients undergoing prehospital pleural decompression within a physician-led HEMS between January 2018 and December 2024, managed with PHMT or PHCD according to clinical judgment. The primary outcome, scene time, was analyzed using Bayesian robust Student-t regression; recorded complications and survival were analyzed using Bayesian beta-binomial models, with posterior risk differences and credible intervals. Ninety-four patients were included (66 PHMT; 28 PHCD). After excluding two implausible zero-minute scene-time records, the posterior median difference in scene time was -5.9 min (95% credible interval [CrI], -13.8 to 1.7; 94.0% probability PHMT was shorter). Complication status was evaluable in 50/66 PHMT and 10/28 PHCD patients. Recorded complications occurred in 0/50 evaluable PHMT and 6/10 evaluable PHCD patients (risk difference -58.7 percentage points, 95% CrI -83.9 to -29.3; probability >99.9% that recorded complications were less frequent with PHMT). Prehospital survival was lower with PHMT, reflecting greater baseline severity, whereas no clear differences were observed at 1, 30, or 90 days. Prehospital minithoracostomy was not associated with longer scene time and was associated with fewer recorded complications than PHCD. Because allocation was nonrandomized, complication ascertainment differed between procedures, and few events occurred, these findings are hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of comparative safety. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized indications and systematic outcome assessment are warranted.

articles.title: Development and independent regional validation of a dynamic ultrasound appendicitis score for suspected acute appendicitis: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract: Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency. Although CT is highly accurate, radiation exposure is a major concern in children, young adults, and pregnant women. Ultrasound is radiation-free but operator-dependent, and current scores rely on static weights without accounting for important patient-finding interactions. To develop and independently validate a Dynamic Ultrasound Appendicitis Score (Dynamic UAS) with interaction effects to improve risk stratification and potentially avoid unnecessary CT examinations. A prospective multicenter study collected development (n = 802) and independent regional external validation (n = 262) data. The Dynamic UAS was derived using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and internally validated using bootstrapping (1000 resamples). A web-based calculator was developed. A sensitivity analysis addressed limitations of the reference standard, non-visualized appendix, and missing data. Appendicitis prevalence was 33.3% (development) and 32.8% (validation). The Dynamic UAS performed excellently in diagnosing acute appendicitis (AUC 0.96 and 0.94) and outperformed known scores (AUC 0.81 to 0.91). At the ≥ 6 level, sensitivity was 91.7%/90.7%, and specificity was 97.1%/96.0%. Calibration was good (slope 0.89, Brier 0.098). In non-visualized appendix cases, the AUC was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84 to 0.93) in the external validation cohort and 0.90 (95% CI: 0.85 to 0.94) in the development cohort. The model is not very useful for distinguishing complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis (AUC 0.72). The Dynamic UAS is a novel, independently validated tool that may reduce unnecessary CT use in radiation-sensitive populations and resource-limited settings. Future studies in different international settings are needed.

articles.title: Three doors, three locks: a domain-specific framework for the residual door-to-balloon gap in STEMI care : Matters Arising, commentary on Krishnan et al., Int J Emerg Med 2026;19:113.
articles.abstract: Krishnan and colleagues report that 91% of STEMI patients at a large Indian tertiary centre received primary PCI within the 90-minute door-to-balloon (D2B) target, a meaningful achievement in contemporary STEMI care. Their analysis of the 9% who missed the target is equally valuable: delays distributed almost evenly across three categories, delayed informed consent, hemodynamic instability, and diagnostic ambiguity. We argue these categories are not interchangeable quality-improvement targets. They are mechanistically distinct problems requiring different solutions. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated taxonomy. Future STEMI quality improvement efforts should categorize residual delays by domain rather than reporting them in aggregate, and should match interventions to the specific mechanism of delay.

articles.title: Securing Medical Countermeasures in Public Health Emergencies.
Layered risk factors for sudden unexpected infant death.
articles.abstract: Sudden Unexpected Infant Death occurs about once a week in Cook County, Illinois, the second largest county in the United States, where SUID disproportionately affects families from high hardship communities. The Cook County SUID Case Registry was established in 2019 to collect, analyze, and disseminate data to advance SUID prevention. Cook County SUID Case Registry data from 2019 to 2023 were analyzed for descriptive characteristics including infant age, race, ethnicity, gestational age, birth weight, maternal age, prenatal/household smoke exposure, and sleep environment hazards. Case reviews (including narrative review) identified patterns of risk which were quantified to provide proportions of SUID that occurred among families with histories of domestic violence, substance use, and among families whose infant died when they were away from their usual home ("temporary stays"). SUID that occurred among preterm infants during temporary stays were further analyzed to detail risk among this population. From 2019 to 2023, 208 sleep-related infant deaths occurred in Cook County, Illinois. These deaths peaked at 1-2 months of age. The rate among non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic infants was 14 and 2.3 times that of white infants respectively. Most sleep-related infant deaths involved unsafe sleep situations including a sleep surface other than a crib/bassinet [175/208 (84%)], surface sharing [135/206 (66%)], and soft bedding in the sleep environment [190/205 (93%)]. Families whose infants died experienced social challenges including histories of domestic violence [32/182 (18%)], maternal substance use [53/185 (29%)] and temporary stays outside of the usual home [34/208 (16%)]. Preterm infants who died during temporary stays [12/34 (35%)] had multiple sleep environment hazards [non-supine sleep (4/12, 33%), non-approved sleep surface (12/12,100%), surface sharing (10/11, 91%), soft bedding (12/12,100%)] and social challenges [histories of domestic violence (3/12, 25%), maternal substance use (5/12, 42%) and child welfare involvement (9/12, 75%)]. SUID in Cook County is closely tied to complex social issues and high hardship resulting in layered risk for vulnerable infants. Future work is needed to better understand how these challenges translate into unsafe sleep situations. Preventing SUID connected to these issues necessitates approaches that engage and equip families alongside trusted partners within communities most impacted by sleep-related infant death.

articles.title: Inpatient Outcomes in a SARS-CoV-2 Naïve Population Achieving High Vaccination Coverage Preceding Planned Virus Entry: A Prospective, Natural Experiment, Pandemic Response Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: On November 23, 2021, South Australia lifted border restrictions allowing passive entry of COVID-19 cases into the community. On this date the adult South Australian population was highly vaccinated and COVID-19 naïve (prior infection rate <1:1000). There are no previous outcome data following introduction of SARS-CoV-2 to a susceptible population that was highly vaccinated. The aim of this study was to measure the effect of sole vaccine-derived immunity against SARS-CoV-2, in a virus-naïve population without prior community transmission. This retrospective cohort study of 132,579 adults with COVID-19 was conducted between November 2021 and March 2022. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes were hospital and intensive care unit admission, stratified by vaccination status. Risk-adjusted multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed using a Bayesian framework. Unvaccinated patients had increased odds of death (OR 3.78, 95% credible interval [CrI] 1.20 to 10.58, Bayesian probability of effect [Pr] 0.99), hospital admission (OR 23.9, 95% CrI 19.38 to 29.13, Pr 1.0), and ICU admission (OR 4.68, 95% CrI 1.58 to 12.34, Pr 1.0). Exclusively vaccine-derived immunity against SARS-CoV-2 is unequivocally protective against hospitalization and death. South Australia's pandemic response may be informative in planning for future pandemics, and management of future variants of SARS-CoV-2.

articles.title: Perspectives on and Utility of DNA Data and Facial Recognition Technologies to Aid Postdisaster Family Reunifications.
articles.abstract: Following a disaster, each passing hour and day of family separation erodes children's health and wellbeing. Hospital networks must prioritize expeditious reunifications while safeguarding children, yet despite advances in biometric technologies and data protection, healthcare systems and disaster response organizations are unprepared to integrate biometric tools into postdisaster family reunification strategies. Biometric data (eg, fingerprints, facial images, dental records, DNA data) are deployed routinely for postmortem disaster victim identifications; however, deployment for family reunifications, such as in hospital settings, is hindered by access challenges, technological limitations, and perceived risks. Although DNA kinship analysis is particularly valuable for reunification, not only for postmortem identifications but also for reconnecting genetic relatives, especially children who cannot self-identify, varying attitudes towards biometrics may limit its use. Understanding discomfort with biometric technologies among families and healthcare providers is critical to their effective deployment for reunifications. We therefore sought to (1) assess perceived utility of and willingness to use biometric data in varied postdisaster contexts and (2) identify postdisaster family separation scenarios where biometric technologies could be beneficial. Using child separation vignettes featuring varied disaster types, scales, and timelines, we surveyed 364 caregivers and 131 healthcare providers in the Chicago area. The results showed general support for the use of DNA and facial recognition technology in postdisaster family reunifications. In parallel, we documented real-life separation scenarios, capturing key factors influencing the utility of biometric tools. Findings suggest that disaster preparedness that considers the potential for family separation must include strategies to effectively use biometric data to assist reunifications, in accordance with the best interests of the child.

articles.title: The Influence of Crisis and Risk Communication Best Practices on COVID-19 Communication: A Content Analysis of Lessons Learned and Recommendations.
articles.abstract: Despite the availability of crisis and risk communication best practices, scholars have analyzed and described the global COVID-19 pandemic communication failures that led to mass confusion about disease dynamics and appropriate protective behaviors. In this study, we sought to understand the alignment of crisis and risk communication best practices with national and international organizational lessons learned from COVID-19 pandemic responses. Our study design was a summative content analysis of a purposeful sample of COVID-19 lessons learned and recommendations reports published by US or international organizations between March 2020 and June 2024. Forty-four organizations published 61 reports, with 331 recommendations (24%) aligned with communication strategies, practices, behaviors, or actions. We identified 612 full or partial statements that aligned with at least 1 of 12 crisis and risk communication best practices. Alignment between the 12 crisis and risk communication best practices and report recommendations varied by best practice. "Take a process approach" was the best practice that aligned most frequently with recommendations and "explain risk in plain language" and show "an ethic of care" were the least frequently aligned with recommendations. Word cloud analyses showed alignment between best practice definitions and report recommendations. Our findings indicate that despite the critical nature of the work to inform the public, there is little international consensus on the use of 12 crisis and risk communication best practices that represent consolidated evidence about what works. Organizations' own reports and our analysis provide the blueprint for future robust crisis and risk communication emergency responses, if the organizations heed their own advice. We recommend that in advance of the next pandemic, organizations at all levels prioritize building awareness of and planning with these 12 best practices so they are prepared to fully listen to and respond to public's information needs.

articles.title: The Regional Disaster Health Response System: A Successful Model to Improve Healthcare Preparedness.
articles.abstract: The Regional Disaster Health Response System (RDHRS) first began in 2018 as a demonstration project designed to address persistent healthcare emergency preparedness and response challenges in the United States. Four RDHRS programs currently exist, aligning and improving healthcare disaster response plans and clinical capabilities across 24 of the 50 US states. They connect public and private partners across the healthcare continuum, ensuring healthcare systems are better prepared for the next catastrophic disaster impacting health systems and the communities they serve. As a convener and a center of specialty expertise, the RDHRS crosses healthcare system and jurisdictional boundaries to address the most significant regional healthcare preparedness and response needs, helping the nation be better prepared to care for the ill and injured in the next large-scale event or disaster. The program has demonstrated its value and success in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2022 pediatric tripledemic, intravenous supply disruption and shortage issues in 2024, and other regional healthcare emergencies, such as chemical incidents, while also improving plans and readiness for other potential threats such as mass burn events. Because the need for, and benefit of, an RDHRS program has been demonstrated through these recent events, there is a need to expand the network to cover the entire nation, further increasing healthcare readiness and our collective abilities to mitigate health system surge and respond to the next catastrophic emergency.

articles.title: MRI of acute appendicitis in pregnancy: navigating diagnostic pitfalls and challenges.
articles.abstract: Non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the preferred cross-sectional imaging modality for suspected appendicitis in pregnancy, yet its interpretation is uniquely challenging. This pictorial review moves beyond simple appendiceal diameter thresholds to the practical pitfalls encountered in daily practice. We show how the enlarging gravid uterus displaces the appendix and how physiologic changes mask inflammatory signs. We also address the diagnostic uncertainty of the equivocal appendix and the need to recognize subtle secondary features on MRI. We then detail several important entities that may confound interpretation, either by mimicking an inflamed appendix or by obscuring a normal one: pelvic venous engorgement, terminal ileitis, cecal diverticulitis, ovarian torsion, and ectopic pregnancy. For each, we highlight the features that help distinguish them. Finally, we discuss technical limitations such as field inhomogeneity and motion artifacts. We present a stepwise approach to locating the appendix paired with a problem-solving strategy that combines non-fat-suppressed and fat-suppressed T2-weighted sequences. By recognizing these multifaceted pearls and pitfalls, radiologists can improve diagnostic confidence and optimize care in this challenging population.

articles.title: Strangulated Posterior Rectus Sheath Hernia with Contained Small-Bowel Perforation and Abdominal Wall Necrotizing Infection: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Posterior rectus sheath hernia is an exceptionally uncommon interparietal hernia and may be difficult to recognize because the herniated bowel remains between abdominal wall layers. A 49-year-old multiparous woman presented with acute severe pain, vomiting, fever, and inflammatory skin changes over a right paraumbilical swelling that had been present for six years. Ultrasound suggested a complicated abdominal wall cyst, whereas computed tomography demonstrated a right rectus sheath hernia. Emergency exploration revealed strangulated and perforated small bowel contained between rectus sheath layers, with enteric leakage into necrotic anterior abdominal wall tissues. Approximately 20 cm of gangrenous bowel was resected and a primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The small fascial defect was closed primarily without mesh because of the dirty infected field. The skin and subcutaneous wound were left open after debridement, managed with temporary packing and two further operative debridements, and closed secondarily after infection control. The patient recovered and was discharged in good clinical condition. Posterior rectus sheath hernia should be considered in atypical abdominal wall masses. Early computed tomography and urgent source control are essential when strangulation, perforation, or necrotizing infection is suspected.

articles.title: Early-Phase Computed Tomography Bowel Diameter and Neurological Outcomes Post-Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
articles.abstract: We aimed to conduct an exploratory investigation on the association between bowel diameter on early-phase abdominal computed tomography (CT) and neurological outcomes in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). This observational study included patients who underwent ECPR for OHCA and abdominal CT before intensive care unit admission between January 2015 and December 2021 at a tertiary emergency medical center. Maximum bowel diameter was measured with a picture archiving and communication system by an investigator blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was unfavorable neurological outcomes at 1 month, defined as Cerebral Performance Category 3-5. The discriminatory ability of bowel diameter was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Data from 181 patients were analyzed (median age, 57 years; 84.5% male). Bowel diameter demonstrated a weak ability to predict unfavorable neurological outcomes, with an AUC of 0.58 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47-0.70). However, higher discriminatory performance was observed in subgroups of patients aged ≥ 65 years (AUC, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69-0.96) and those with initial nonshockable rhythms (AUC, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.47-0.91). The results of this exploratory investigation suggest that bowel diameter may represent a potential adjunctive marker associated with functional outcomes post-ECPR for OHCA.
